concept.name: Revenue
concept.definition: The total amount of money a company brings in from selling its products or services during a period, before any expenses are deducted - the 'top line' of the income statement. It is typically reported as net revenue after subtracting returns, allowances, and discounts.
concept.intuition: Revenue is the raw scale of a business's sales engine; every margin and profit figure ultimately starts from it.
concept.mechanics: Companies recognize revenue when performance obligations are satisfied - goods delivered or services rendered - under GAAP or IFRS rules, not necessarily when cash arrives. The income statement then deducts costs stepwise from revenue down to the bottom line.
concept.formula: Net revenue = Gross revenue (sales) - Returns, allowances, and discounts.
concept.failure_modes: Recognition rules leave room for timing games such as channel stuffing, and revenue growth can mask deteriorating economics when margins are collapsing underneath.
concept.misconceptions: Revenue is neither income nor cash: a firm can book large revenue while losing money or burning cash, because expenses and working-capital needs are accounted for elsewhere.
concept.example: Apple reported about $394 billion of net sales in fiscal 2022 against roughly $100 billion of net income; the $294 billion gap is cost of sales, operating expenses, interest, and taxes.

citations.source: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Beginners' Guide to Financial Statements
